findings.text: the head gate log records only its revision and omits the tree, the module under test and the command or file set its base arm records, so a reader cannot confirm from the log alone that the same seven files ran and the 39-to-41 delta rests on the manifest's prose.

the rewritten comment says every launch sits behind the overlay, but reckon/crew/resumption.py:248 composes the lane-availability probe with fence=False, so the sentence holds for worker launches only and a reader auditing the guarantee cannot tell from the comment that the probe is exempt deliberately.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against b11cf190 - d7ba7433 carries the flag, its rewritten guarantee comment and the new test, and 01327c5b the landing record, archive anchor, figure and logs; the diff is eight files, all inside the declared scope, including a disclosed repair of an unclosed paragraph tag in the archive, which I confirmed was open at base around its line 1379.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names seven test files and two arms; I re-ran tests/test_fence_is_on_again.py at the reviewed head (2 passed) and read both recorded arms - gate-fence-is-on-again-head.txt (41 passed at d7ba7433) and gate-fence-is-on-again-base.txt (39 passed at b11cf190 with the flag forced false) - and the new default is asserted through the composed dispatch path, not only on the constant.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to launch crew workers fenced again by setting FENCE_WORKERS true; reckon/crew/dispatch.py:135 carries FENCE_WORKERS = True at the reviewed head, and I confirmed each of the four preconditions it names (80d55621, 29a30fb1, 3db08a97, e562d32e) is an ancestor of the base b11cf190.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names both commits, the two gate arms, the turned-off disclosure and three follow-ons, and every log it names resolves in both the run directory and docs/figures.
item_verdicts.write_paths: I read the eight declared paths from the node prompt; all eight files of the diff lie inside them, the six pre-existing section 2 test files are byte-identical to base, and no path outside the declaration was touched.

justifications.durability: tests/test_fence_is_on_again.py:126 fails if the flag returns to False, and the composed-argv case at lines 151, 155 and 161 reddens with the flag off as the executed control shows; the harness-home assertion at :155 is measured against the run directory the same composition supplies, so that one line is internally consistent rather than absolute.
justifications.evidence: the two arms and the control are recorded at docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/ with the control's first line repeating the declared string verbatim, and I re-ran tests/test_fence_is_on_again.py at the reviewed head (2 passed); the head arm's log omits the tree and file set its base arm records.
justifications.fit: tests/test_fence_is_on_again.py follows the surrounding idiom (pytest_plugins from tests.test_crew, a synthetic operator home and repository, a __main__ control block) and introduces no plan, sprint or version identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:135 sets FENCE_WORKERS to True at the head and the four precondition commits the goal names all resolve as ancestors of b11cf190, so a worker launch composes through the fence as the goal states.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status b11cf190..01327c5b lists only the declared paths - dispatch.py, the new test, the plan page, the archive and the figures directory - and the six other section 2 test files are byte-identical to base.
